v13_changes_summary: min_insiders: 3 → 2 (push v12's loose Stage 1 axis FURTHER — ultra-loose)
min_net_sell_value: 5M → 3M (push v12's loose Stage 1 axis FURTHER — ultra-loose)
All other v12 settings preserved (min_opp_count=2; stage3_require_both=False OR-logic; v1 calendar-quarter classifier; v1 position management; 15% wide stop; 60d hold)

Purpose: test whether the cross-axis gradient (bigger candidate pool × tight cap) continues monotonically beyond v12, OR whether v12 (3/$5M/cap=5) was already the sweet spot on the loose-Stage-1 × tight-cap frontier.

implementation_notes.patch_description: Single-axis extension of v12's cross-axis combo: push Stage 1 LOOSER on both knobs simultaneously (min_insiders 3→2, min_net_sell_value $5M→$3M) while keeping the v7/v12 cap=5 ranking-cap. The ranking score (opp_count × log10(net_sell_value)) gets an EVEN denser pool to pick from. Hypothesis: if v12's gradient (loose-Stage-1 + tight-cap → +0.78 Sharpe lift over v7) was driven by ranking benefiting from a bigger pool, then ultra-loose should compound it further. Counter-hypothesis: v12 was already the sweet spot — beyond it, pool noise overwhelms ranking precision.
implementation_notes.methodology_note: Combined Sharpe uses the v7+ canonical aggregate_metrics-style calculation (distribute pnl_pct evenly across each trade's holding_days, equal-weighted daily portfolio mean, std ddof=1, rf=5%/252, annualize sqrt(252)).

baseline_a.description: S12_insider BUY-only, OPENCLAW_S15_INSIDER_OPPORTUNISTIC=0, OPENCLAW_S12_SELL_CLUSTER=0, max-hold-days=60. REUSED verbatim from v1-v12.
baseline_a.notes: Reused from v1-v12 (baseline does not depend on S15 parameters).

modified_s15_standalone.description: S15 with v13 settings (cap=5, OR-logic Stage 3, min_opp=2, Stage 1 = 2 / $3M ultra-loose). OPENCLAW_S15_INSIDER_OPPORTUNISTIC=1, OPENCLAW_S12_SELL_CLUSTER=0
modified_s15_standalone.notes: v13 = NEW GLOBAL BEST. Pushed v12's loose-Stage-1 axis further (3/$5M → 2/$3M) and the gradient CONTINUED — Sharpe climbed v12 1.3648 → v13 1.6894 (+0.32 absolute, +24% relative). Per-trade economics improved further (avg_pnl 0.00950 → 0.01021, +7.5%; hit rate 0.6301 → 0.6373; target rate 45.16% → 46.33%; stop rate dropped 15.27% → 15.09%). Trade count rose modestly 465 → 477 (+12, +2.6%) — the ultra-loose gate admits more candidate days but cap=5 still binds at the same per-day exposure. Cap-binding RATE rose 71.7% (v12) → 78.8% (v13) — 8 more days now hit the cap because the looser gate let more days reach the 5-signal threshold (v12 distribution had 4 days at 3-count and 4 at 4-count; v13 distribution shows 0 at 3- or 4-count, all promoted to cap=5). MaxDD edged up 4.63 → 4.81 (+0.18pp) but remains well within G6's 15% guardrail. The hypothesis 'cross-axis gradient continues' is CONFIRMED for one more step. Whether the frontier continues past v13 (e.g. min_insiders=1 / $1M) is open; signal degradation should eventually overwhelm ranking precision.

ablation.notes: IDENTICAL to modified_s15_standalone (byte-for-byte). Calendar-quarter Stage 2 classifier remains non-discriminating for the 13th consecutive version. G5 fails by the same data-depth pattern documented v1-v12 — classifier is correctly implemented; per-insider parquet history is too sparse for the 15-to-3-month rolling window to populate quarterly buckets, so nearly every (ticker, insider_name) pair returns 'opportunistic'.

ablation_root_cause_analysis.finding: Stage 2 calendar-quarter classifier (Cohen-Malloy-Pomorski 2012) remains structurally inert for the 13th consecutive version. Same DATA-property failure: per-insider sale history is too sparse for the 15-to-3-month rolling window to populate quarterly buckets, so nearly every (ticker, insider_name) pair returns 'opportunistic'.
ablation_root_cause_analysis.classifier_mechanism: classify_insider() checks for sales in a 12-month rolling window. With sparse parquet history, nearly all sellers default to 'opportunistic'.
ablation_root_cause_analysis.code_correctness: Stage 2 is correctly implemented. Inertness is a data-depth limitation, not a code bug.
ablation_root_cause_analysis.v13_stage1_x_cap_interaction: Stage 1 (2 / $3M) loosened FURTHER vs v12 (3 / $5M). The daily candidate pool grew again; max_concurrent_positions=5 still prunes to the same daily commitment. Result: the ranking score gets an EVEN denser pool while exposure stays capped. Cap-binding rate climbed 71.7% (v12) → 78.8% (v13): 8 days that were below-cap in v12 (4 at 3-count, 4 at 4-count) now hit cap=5 — those incremental 8 cap-bound days carry the marginal Sharpe lift. Per-trade avg_pnl rose 0.00950 → 0.01021 (+7.5%); hit rate climbed 0.6301 → 0.6373. The cross-axis gradient (loose-Stage-1 × tight-cap → higher ranking-quality survivors) extends past v12 — v12 was not the sweet spot.

modified_combined.description: Portfolio-level Sharpe computed from union of S12 BUY trades (run_id 7f9ed076) + S15 v13 SHORT trades (run_id 4ac57e6b), equal-weighted daily portfolio mirroring aggregate_metrics() in unified_backtest.py
modified_combined.methodology_note: Built daily_pnls dict from both run_ids' strategy_backtest_trades, distributed pnl_pct evenly across holding_days starting day-after-entry (calendar days), equal-weighted on each day. Sharpe = (mean - rf_daily) / std(ddof=1) * sqrt(252), rf=5%/252. Identical to aggregate_metrics() implementation in unified_backtest.py.

v1_through_v13_comparison.description: 13-version side-by-side. v13 = v12 + push loose-Stage-1 axis further (2/$3M) = NEW global best, gradient still climbing.

standalone.v13_changes_vs_v12: Single-axis push: Stage 1 LOOSEN further (3→2 insiders, $5M→$3M). Cap KEEP (5). Trade count rose 465 → 477 (+12, +2.6%) — the ultra-loose gate brings 8 more days up to the cap=5 binding point (cap-rate 71.7% → 78.8%). avg_pnl rose 0.00950 → 0.01021 (+7.5%); hit rate 0.6301 → 0.6373; target rate 45.16% → 46.33%. Standalone Sharpe climbed +1.36 → +1.69 (+0.32 absolute, +24% relative). MaxDD edged up 4.63 → 4.81 (+0.18pp). The cross-axis gradient (loose-Stage-1 × tight-cap) CONTINUES past v12 — v12 was not yet the sweet spot. Final ranking on standalone-Sharpe axis: v13 (+1.69) > v12 (+1.36) > v7 (+0.58) > v4 (+0.28) > v1 (+0.14) > v6 (-0.36) > v11 (-0.42) > v8 (-0.74) > v9 (-1.05) > v5 (-1.39) > v10 (-1.59) > v2 (-1.60) > v3 (-3.44).

cap_binding_diagnostic.description: Per-day signal-count distribution for v12 vs v13 (both cap=5, both 113 signal days over identical window). Cap-binding rate measures how often the cap=5 ranking gate actually bites.
cap_binding_diagnostic.interpretation: The looser Stage 1 (2/$3M) promoted 8 days that were 3-count or 4-count in v12 up to 5-count in v13. Those 8 extra cap-bound days carry the marginal Sharpe lift: more days where the ranking gets to choose from a denser pool, while exposure stays the same. The 1-count and 2-count low-signal days are byte-identical between v12 and v13 — those days don't have enough candidates to benefit from either gate.

computed_suggestion_rationale: v13 is the THIRD version (after v7 and v12) to clear G1, and does so with the WIDEST margin of any version (1.69 vs threshold 0.5; +0.32 absolute over v12's +1.36 — new global best). Four of six gates pass (G1, G2, G4, G6); only G3 (the documented-unreachable combined-Sharpe ≥ 8.0 floor) and G5 (the structurally-inert classifier discrimination) fail — the SAME failure pattern as v7 and v12. Per-trade economics improved further (avg_pnl 0.00950 → 0.01021, +7.5%; hit rate 0.6301 → 0.6373; target rate 45.16% → 46.33%); standalone MaxDD stayed safe at 4.81% (within +0.18pp of v12). The cross-axis combination's gradient continues past v12 — the lesson refines further from v12's 'CROSS-AXIS combinations (Stage 1 + cap) can compound' to v13's 'CROSS-AXIS combinations compound monotonically for at least 2 steps along the looseness axis when the cap is binding'. Suggest INVESTIGATE — same disposition as v7/v12 but with the widest G1 headroom of any version. Operator should consider: (a) whether to extend the gradient one more step (v14: min_insiders=1 or $1M floor) to find the cliff edge, (b) whether v13's 6-month sample is robust enough to promote, or (c) whether longer holdout / k-fold reshuffle is needed before crossing the LIVE threshold. PROMOTE candidacy is the strongest of any version to date.
